description: Archetype brief templates used by `tools-offline-app-dev.py brief`. Placeholders {ref}, {name}, {category}, {description} are substituted at generation time. Editing this file changes the generated briefs; keep section names stable.
brief_note: Briefs are deterministic work orders. They do not execute the catalog concept; they make it actionable with pinned inputs, offline boundaries, and verification steps.

implement.label: Focused reusable capability
implement.contract: Declared inputs and outputs, pinned dependencies, offline behavior, security boundaries, tests, diagnostics, documentation, and cross-platform acceptance criteria.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.body: Implement {name} as a focused, reusable capability (catalog {ref}, category: {category}). {description}

sections.heading: Declared inputs
sections.body:
- Explicit configuration object (schema versioned, all paths relative, no ambient environment reads)
- Pinned dependency manifest and local cache/lockfile (no implicit network fetch)
- Target platform identifier and minimum OS/API level
- Workload parameters and permission grants required by the platform

sections.heading: Declared outputs
sections.body:
- Deterministic result artifact(s) written to an explicit output path
- Structured diagnostics (JSON) with severity, code, message, remediation hint
- Test evidence (unit + contract) tied to the acceptance criteria below

sections.heading: Offline boundary
sections.body:
- All dependencies restored from the local offline bundle/cache with hashes verified
- No hidden first-run downloads; any provisioning step fails fast with a clear offline error
- Optional networked features degrade gracefully and are verified separately in controlled connected environments

sections.heading: Security boundaries
sections.body:
- Least-privilege: request only the platform permissions required
- No secrets, keys, or credentials in source or fixtures; inject at runtime from the platform keystore/secret store
- Inputs validated before use; untrusted data never reaches privileged APIs unchecked

sections.heading: Tests
sections.body:
- Unit tests for pure logic (offline)
- Contract tests per supported platform (mocked adapters permitted)
- Negative-path tests: missing dependency, denied permission, corrupt cache, read-only target
- Diagnostics emit actionable codes; documentation lists every code and its remediation

sections.heading: Cross-platform acceptance criteria
sections.body:
- Same public interface on every supported target; platform specifics hidden behind the interface
- Behavior parity verified on at least one simulator/emulator and one physical device per mobile target
- Documented escape hatch to the native API for platform-only needs

evaluate.label: Pass/warn/fail evaluation
evaluate.contract: Clean, reproducible evaluation with explicit pass, warn, and fail criteria; retain target platform, toolchain version, device or simulator, observed result, failure evidence, and exact remediation and retest steps.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.body: Evaluate {name} (catalog {ref}, category: {category}) in a clean, reproducible environment. {description}

sections.heading: Required recorded context
sections.body:
- Target platform, OS version, and architecture
- Toolchain and SDK versions (exact, pinned)
- Device, simulator, or emulator model and OS image
- Date, operator, and source revision of the build under test

sections.heading: Pass / warn / fail criteria
sections.body:
- PASS: observed result meets the criterion with margin; evidence attached
- WARN: criterion met with degradation or advisory; document, schedule, and retest trigger defined
- FAIL: criterion not met; capture failure evidence (logs, screenshots, traces) and exact remediation steps
- UNTESTED: no result recorded; never silently counted as pass

sections.heading: Evidence retention
sections.body:
- Store raw logs, screenshots, and profiler/trace output beside the report
- Record the exact retest command and expected result after remediation
- Keep reports immutable; supersede with a new report rather than editing history

sections.heading: Environment cleanliness
sections.body:
- Evaluate on a clean machine or reset VM/container; network blocked for offline criteria
- Restore from the pinned offline bundle; verify integrity before the run
- No leftover state from previous runs (clear app data, fresh install)

adapter.label: Stable-interface platform adapter
adapter.contract: Behind a stable interface with capability detection, permission handling, mocked offline tests, platform-specific implementations, graceful degradation, and contract tests for every supported target.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.body: Provide {name} behind a stable interface (catalog {ref}, category: {category}). {description}

sections.heading: Stable interface
sections.body:
- Interface defined once, platform-agnostic (types, errors, async semantics)
- Versioned contract; additive changes only within a major version
- Capability descriptor reported at runtime: name, version, features supported, requires-permission list

sections.heading: Capability detection and graceful degradation
sections.body:
- Detect hardware/OS capability before first use; never assume availability
- When absent: disable the feature with a documented fallback path, not a crash
- Denial of permission yields a typed error + rationale UI hook, never an infinite prompt

sections.heading: Permission handling
sections.body:
- Request at the latest responsible moment with a user-facing rationale
- Handle granted/denied/restricted states distinctly (platform rules differ)
- Re-check on resume; permissions can be revoked while the app is backgrounded

sections.heading: Implementations and tests
sections.body:
- One platform-specific implementation per supported target; shared logic factored out
- Mocked offline tests run without devices; contract tests run per target (emulator/device/hardware)
- Escape hatch: documented accessor to the native API for target-specific needs, clearly marked unstable

build.label: Pinned-input builder
build.contract: From pinned local inputs with integrity checks, deterministic paths, rollback or cleanup behavior, platform-specific metadata, and a post-build install, open, or verification test that requires no hidden download.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.body: Create {name} from pinned local inputs (catalog {ref}, category: {category}). {description}

sections.heading: Inputs and integrity
sections.body:
- Every input pinned by version and SHA-256 (offline bundle manifest)
- Verify hashes before any step runs; abort atomically on mismatch
- Deterministic output paths derived from the config; no timestamps leaking into reproducible artifacts where the platform permits

sections.heading: Rollback and cleanup
sections.body:
- Stage outputs in a temporary sibling directory; publish by atomic rename only after all checks pass
- On failure: remove partial outputs, restore previous state, print recovery instructions
- Never mutate the input bundle in place

sections.heading: Platform-specific metadata
sections.body:
- Stamp artifacts with platform metadata required for install/launch (version, SDK/min-OS, arch, signing identity placeholder, package id)
- Keep signing material outside the build inputs; reference it by handle/alias only

sections.heading: Post-build verification
sections.body:
- Automatic install-or-open smoke test on a local device/simulator/emulator, or equivalent headless check
- The verification requires no hidden download; it must pass on a network-blocked clean machine
- Record verification evidence beside the artifact (checksum manifest, log, verdict)

operate.label: Long-running managed operation
operate.contract: Versioned configuration, bounded resource use, deterministic state transitions, cancellation and recovery paths, structured errors, and platform-specific fallbacks that preserve user data.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.body: Operate {name} as a managed, recoverable capability (catalog {ref}, category: {category}). {description}

sections.heading: Versioned configuration
sections.body:
- Configuration schema carries an explicit version; migrations are forward-only with backup
- Unknown keys are rejected or ignored per policy, never silently misread
- Defaults are safe, offline-first, and documented

sections.heading: Bounded resource use
sections.body:
- Explicit limits: memory, disk, concurrency, retry count, and wall-clock timeout
- Backpressure or rejection when saturated; never unbounded queues
- Resource exhaustion produces a typed, actionable error

sections.heading: State transitions and cancellation
sections.body:
- Deterministic state machine: idle -> running -> (succeeded | failed | cancelled); transitions logged
- Cancellation is cooperative, prompt, and leaves no corrupt state (atomic commits or journal)
- Recovery path documented for every failure state; user data always preserved

sections.heading: Errors and fallbacks
sections.body:
- Structured errors: stable code, human message, remediation hint, correlation id
- Platform-specific fallbacks degrade functionality, never integrity
- Preserve user data above all; partial results are committed or rolled back atomically

plan.label: Owned, verifiable plan
plan.contract: Owners, prerequisites, ordered steps, decision points, failure recovery, required evidence, and a clean completion condition suitable for offline teams and repeatable releases.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.body: Define {name} (catalog {ref}, category: {category}) with owners, prerequisites, ordered steps, decision points, failure recovery, and evidence. {description}

sections.heading: Owners and prerequisites
sections.body:
- Named roles (not just people): accountable owner, reviewer, decider for each decision point
- Prerequisites verified before step 1: pinned toolchain, offline bundle restored, devices/emulators available, prior ADRs reviewed
- Missing prerequisite blocks the plan loudly; no silent skipping

sections.heading: Ordered steps and decision points
sections.body:
- Steps are sequential, each with entry criteria, action, exit criteria, and evidence artifact
- Decision points have explicit options, a decider, and a default taken offline without external input
- Parallelizable steps are marked; dependencies between steps are explicit

sections.heading: Failure recovery
sections.body:
- Every step names its failure modes and the recovery action (retry with backoff / roll back / escalate)
- Rollback restores the last known-good state; data migrations are reversible or dual-written
- Re-plan trigger: any failed gate stops the plan until re-reviewed

sections.heading: Evidence and completion condition
sections.body:
- Required evidence list archived with the release record (logs, reports, checksums, sign-offs)
- Completion condition is objectively checkable (e.g., acceptance checklist all-pass, artifact reproducible)
- Nothing is 'done' on verbal confirmation alone

select-configure.label: Smallest-maintainable selection
select-configure.contract: Select and configure the smallest maintainable solution for the target platforms, documenting compatibility, dependency weight, performance, accessibility, distribution constraints, and escape paths for platform-specific code.

sections.heading: Responsibility
sections.body: Use {name} to select and configure the smallest maintainable solution (catalog {ref}, category: {category}). {description}

sections.heading: Selection method
sections.body:
- Enumerate candidate solutions; prefer the smallest dependency weight that meets hard constraints
- Score against the decision matrix criteria (see asset-decision-matrix.json; override weights via the matrix command)
- Reject any candidate that cannot be restored offline or cannot satisfy the minimum OS/arch targets

sections.heading: Documented decision record
sections.body:
- Compatibility: platforms, minimum OS versions, CPU architectures
- Dependency weight: direct + transitive size, license class, pinning status
- Performance: startup, memory, and binary-size implications with measurement plan
- Accessibility: platform a11y APIs honored (VoiceOver/TalkBack/UI Automation/AT-SPI)
- Distribution constraints: store policies, signing, notarization, update channel, enterprise vs consumer route

sections.heading: Configuration and escape paths
sections.body:
- Minimal configuration checked into source; secrets stay out
- Document the escape path to platform-specific code for anything the abstraction cannot express
- Record the decision as an ADR (see the adr command) so future changes have context
